title: Letter analysis result
description: What /v1/analyze returns for one photographed letter. Used as the model's structured-output schema. The catalogue supplies the key enums, and it is a hint rather than a gate: a document or body it does not carry is returned by its Hebrew name with key null, and is every bit as valid. Keys buy translation into four languages, nothing else. Enum members are injected per request from contracts/catalogue.json plus whatever vocabulary the user has added for themselves. The schema is never hand-edited to add a key; add it to index.html and regenerate the catalogue.

agency.$comment: enum := Object.keys(catalogue.agencies). null when the letter names no agency this app knows.
agency.description: Which body sent the letter, as a catalogue key or a key this user has added. null when neither fits — agency_he then carries the name.

agency_child.$comment: One of catalogue.agencies[agency].children, when the parent is an umbrella (bank, health fund).
agency_child.description: The specific bank or health fund, when the agency is an umbrella entry.

template.$comment: enum := Object.keys(catalogue.templates). null when the letter is about no known process.
template.description: Which known process this letter belongs to, if any.

key.$comment: enum := Object.keys(catalogue.docs) + this user's own doc keys + null.
key.description: A catalogue key when one genuinely fits, which buys four translations. null otherwise — and null is a normal answer, not a failure. A wrong key is worse than no key.

he.description: The document's name in Hebrew, as the letter writes it. Required even when a key matched, because it is what makes a document without a key usable rather than discarded.

evidence.description: The Hebrew phrase in the letter that asks for this document. Quoted, not paraphrased. This is the field that carries the guarantee: the server drops any document it cannot show a quote for, whatever the document is called. It is what separates a list read off the page from a list guessed from the subject.

required_docs.description: Every document the letter asks for, in one list. There used to be a second array for documents with no catalogue key; the split existed only because those were treated as second-class, and they are not.

deadline.$comment: ISO 8601 date. The model resolves relative wording ('תוך 30 יום') against letter_date, and returns null rather than guessing when letter_date is unreadable.

letter_date.description: The date printed on the letter, needed to resolve relative deadlines.

reference.description: The אסמכתא / case number, copied character for character. This is the thing worth arguing with later.

form_code.description: The form or letter code printed on the page — 'בל/250', 'טופס 101', a departmental letter number. Israeli agency correspondence almost always carries one, and it is the cheapest reliable way to recognise a letter as one we have seen before.
form_code.$comment: Impersonal by construction: it identifies the template, not the recipient. The server hashes it with the agency and normalised title into a form_signature, and that signature is the only thing that may be stored.

form_title_he.description: The letter's own heading in Hebrew, verbatim. Second input to the signature, for letters that carry no code.

personalised.description: True when the letter is individual correspondence — a caseworker writing about one person's specific situation — rather than a standard template. A personalised letter is never promoted to the shared catalogue, whatever its signature.

confidence.description: Overall. Below the server threshold the result is returned but the client adds nothing.

language.description: Language the letter is written in. At launch anything but 'he' is returned with a low confidence and no additions.

not_a_letter.description: The image is not an agency letter — a selfie, a receipt, a blurry frame. Set by the Haiku pre-check without reaching the main model.

form_to_fill.description: Whether there is a form the user must fill and submit. 'self' means this same document contains it — a letter with a tear-off section — which is common and is why the client offers to fill without asking for a second scan.

agency_he.description: The body's name in Hebrew, exactly as it appears on the document. Always filled, including when a key matched — a letter may say סניף חיפה and that is worth showing. When no key matched it is the only thing standing between the user and a case filed under "other", and the client offers to save it as a body of their own.
